subject: Lumencare VPC: Support mapping, platform fee floor, and packaging tradeoffs
messages:
From: Sarah King <sarah.king@lumencare.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lumencare.com
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Initial pricing questions for VPC deployment

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the routing/fallback flow. Procurement asked me to get a clearer read on the private deployment economics before we proceed. Two asks to start: 

1) Can you share a simple SKU matrix that maps the on-prem node counts / reserved capacity bands to the platform fee and support tiers (response times / oncall hours)?
2) What flexibility do you have on the platform fee floor for a 3-year commit? We need to model a baseline OPEX for our finance team.

Also, our security team asked about a discrete SOW for installation and a clear oncall handoff process (who owns emergency oncall first 90 days).

Appreciate anything you can share.

Best,
Sarah King
Head of Infrastructure, LumenCare Inc.

---
Attachment: (none in first message)
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah King <sarah.king@lumencare.com>, procurement@lumencare.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 12:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial pricing questions for VPC deployment

Hi Sarah — great to hear the demo resonated. I’m attaching a concise SKU matrix and a support-tiers CSV that maps response/onsite windows to the support tranche. High level: 

- SKU matrix includes Starter / Standard / Enterprise nodes, with optional burst capacity; platform fee is quoted as a monthly floor + per-node metered component.
- For 3-year commitments we can consider a stepped platform fee where the first 12 months have an implementation discount.

I’ve looped in Marissa (pricing) to suggest what a realistic concession looks like for a 36-month commit; Diego is on our delivery team and will draft the installation SOW with the handoff language.

Attachments: Lumencare_VPC_SKUs_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB), Support_Tiers_Table.csv (CSV, 8KB)

Proposed next step: internal discussion to surface target ARR/commitment number and preferred support SLA from your side, then I’ll put together a one-page term summary. Can you share the finance team’s target annual spend bands?

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Lumencare_VPC_SKUs_v2.xlsx; Support_Tiers_Table.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Lumencare VPC pricing — internal reco

Rohan / Diego — quick internal note before we push numbers out: 

- Lumencare looks like a mid-market health customer. If they sign 36 months and guarantee an average monthly commit >= $45k we can reduce the platform fee floor by 18% compared to standard list.
- To protect unit economics, require a 12-month ramp with a 10% minimum utilization floor (in SOW).
- For support: we can offer Tier 2 (4-hr P1, business-hours P2) as standard; Tier 1 (1-hr P1, 24/7 oncall) should be priced as an add-on unless they commit to an elevated retainer.

Diego — for the SOW draft include: 90-day joint runbook, 2x on-call handoff sessions, and optional 24/7 paid escalation. If they ask for platform fee below the 18% concession, push for a longer commit or an increased node minimum.

I’ll backfill with modeled ARR impact and an approval ask for a one-time implementation credit (up to 5% of first-year platform fee) if we need to compete.

-Marissa
Director, Commercial Pricing
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

(Internal message; no external recipients)
From: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@lumencare.com>

Cc: Sarah King <sarah.king@lumencare.com>, procurement@lumencare.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial pricing questions for VPC deployment

Thanks Rohan — the attachments are helpful. A few items from procurement/finance after review: 

1) The $45k band is close to our expectations, but finance is asking whether you can move to a 22% platform fee reduction for a strict 36-month commit if we agree to a 15% upfront prepayment. That gets their modeled NPV in range.
2) For support, we need clarity on who owns P1 during the first 90 days. Sarah: legal wants the SOW to say Redwood owns first responder responsibilities up to the delivery acceptance milestone, then joint oncall afterwards. Is that acceptable?
3) We also want a single price for a Starter bundle that includes a small implementation credit, and prefer the SOW to list a deterministic exit window (30 days) and data egress process.

On timing: procurement would like a redlined SOW by Thursday EOD if possible so we can get legal to review next week.

Appreciate you pushing on the platform fee — let me know if that 22% is possible with the prepay.

> Follow-up from our finance team attached — highlighted target bands.

Best,
Aaron Patel

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial pricing questions for VPC deployment — proposed concessions and SOW link

Aaron / Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. Summary of our proposed concession package and next steps: 

1) Platform fee: we can accommodate the 22% reduction off standard list for a 36-month committed ARR with a 15% upfront prepayment. That concession requires the 10% utilization floor in the SOW during the first year and quarterly utilization reporting.

2) Support/SOW: Redwood will be the first responder for P1 incidents up to the delivery acceptance milestone (delineated in the SOW). After acceptance, we move to the joint oncall model described in the support tiers CSV. Diego will own the runbook and will include the 90-day handoff: 2x runbook walkthroughs, defined escalation matrix, and 24/7 paid escalation option.

3) Implementation credit & exit: We will include a one-time implementation credit equal to 4% of the first-year platform fee applied to the Starter bundle. The SOW will also include a 30-day exit/egress process clause with obligations for data return and secure wipe.

I’ve uploaded a redlined SOW draft here for your legal review: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/LumenCare-vpc (SOW_draft_Lumencare_20260714.pdf attached). If you’re aligned, next milestone: procurement signs term sheet and we circulate final SOW for signature.

Attachments: SOW_draft_Lumencare_20260714.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

Let me know if you want a quick call tomorrow to walk legal through the acceptance milestone language.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
